#### 10.7.4.2 R4-G — Inspect OWN Hand outside the active turn, never authorize Play (NEW phone request 2026-10-16)

**Human acceptance: R4-F ACCEPTED/CLOSED on real iPhone, 2026-10-16.** The user confirms the inside-CardFace DETAILS location and compact illustrated card/rules preview now meet the design. Keep R4-F visually and behaviorally unchanged. **Separate new defect R4-G:** nonacting players cannot inspect THEIR OWN Hand CardFaces because the Hand can only be clicked to select an actionable card. **Requirement:** own Hand rules inspection must be available when it is another player's turn or the owner otherwise has no currently authorized action; CONFIRM / PLAY must remain HTML disabled/inert in this inspect-only context. This request does not authorize free off-turn card play and is NOT a renewed failure of R4-F.

**Actual checked code, 2026-10-16 branch ux-v2:**
- In app/page.tsx renderHandCard, maySelect is the current turn/discard OR response/rescue authorization. The physical Hand button uses disabled={!maySelect || skillModeCardDisabled || responseCardDisabled(item)} and cannot be tapped off turn. Its only onClick uses toggleHandCard, which mutates ACTUAL play/discard/skill/response card-choice state.
- The inset hand-card-details-action appears only when selectedHandDetailsCard is non-null; selectedHandDetailsCardId derives from discardSelected, active skill/response costs, Serpent, or selected. An off-turn non-actor has no selection and no DETAILS control.
- The real Local Dock Play/Confirm code already uses room.isMyTurn, currentActionOwnedByViewer and canUseAction on server-projected CurrentAction. These gates must remain. An active legitimate response (Dodge, Attack in Duel, or Negation) may occur on ANOTHER player's turn; its real server-authorized Confirm MUST remain enabled when valid. Off-turn is NOT equivalent to unauthorized.

**Design: two independent modes, never mixed:**

1. **INSPECTION ONLY:** Whenever a started-game viewer has any card legitimately present in their OWN server-projected room.myHand, they can tap it when no applicable actionable card-selection authority exists. It gains a quiet inspect-focus visual and the existing 44x44 in-card DETAILS affordance, which opens the already-accepted compact real CardFace + canonical rule description. Tapping another own card switches inspect focus; DETAILS closes via current close/Escape/return-focus behaviors. Keep Hand sideways scrolling and overlap. Use their real server-known card ID, no new public reveal or other-player Hand access.
2. **ACTION MODE:** When the viewer is genuinely server-authorized to choose a card for Play, Discard, Dodge/Negation/Duel response, rescue, triggered skill/card costs or other active action, keep existing selection flows and eligibility tests intact. Genuine off-turn response cards can be selected and submitted. A disabled game-action card may still be inspected without selecting it for an action; never call an action handler merely because its face is viewable.
3. **Separate state and semantics:** Add a local inspectOnlyHandCardId (or equivalent) distinct from selected, discardSelected, serpentSelected, activeSkillSelectionState, responseProviderId and targetIds. It MUST NOT feed action selection counts, selection validity, CurrentAction, consolePrimaryCandidates, any server-request payload or actual selected cardIds. Rendering uses action-selected card DETAILS if available; otherwise uses inspection focus only when not action-selecting. Mark inspect focus separately (for example data-card-inspect-focused=true, data-card-selected=false) and preserve honest aria-pressed=false for ACTION selection in inspect-only mode. The inspect button has a meaningful accessible label such as Inspect Attack. Do not use aria-pressed=true to falsely claim a playable selection.
4. **Absolutely no off-turn actions:** In inspect-only mode Play/Confirm never becomes actionable. Keep all current server-authoritative gates and disabled states; if a primary action is already visible, it must have native disabled=true and no submit. A low-emphasis disabled Confirm placeholder in an otherwise empty primary slot is OPTIONAL if consistent with existing waiting UI; never add an enabled fake action or a large new toolbar. No effect on End, skill, response or discard permissions. Legitimately authorized off-turn responses must retain working Confirm.
5. **Correct lifecycle/privacy:** Clear inspection focus on viewer/room switch, own-Hand card removal, and transition into a new authorized action; do NOT promote previously inspected card to selected cost automatically. An ordinary same-viewer poll with identical Hand should not collapse the preview. Close an open private preview if ownership/viewer changes or the card leaves room.myHand, without showing an old owner's Hand to a new TEST SWITCH viewer. Never reveal an opponent's hidden hand through public props, logging or reconnect. Server game rules and physical card movement stay unchanged.
6. **Preserve accepted UI:** R4-F's 44x44 inspect hit area remains INSIDE the physical CardFace; **§10.7.4.3 R4-H governs the visible circular `i` appearance instead of the old `DETAILS` rectangle/text**. Same nonmodal art/rules preview with no unnecessary headings and no large backdrop. Protect U13-A's newly delivered multi-discard appearance; inspection focus is NOT action selection or a second discard-selected card. Preserve other publicly inspectable parked CardFaces and equipment previews.

#### 10.8.3 H3 — concise PUBLIC battle announcements with larger, wider, easier-to-read type

**User issue and requested emphasis:** The public battlefield explanation (e.g. Player A uses a card) should be **much easier to read**: larger font, visually wider characters (not compressed/ultra-condensed) and SHORTER truthful content. This builds on delivered UI-3, which already moved the event notice ABOVE the physical centre CardFace and removed redundant result text.

**Final visual contract:**
- During the current card's **large REVEAL**, its factual public event message remains **ABOVE that actual committed physical CardFace**; during card move/park, the message's **independent fixed-stage placement is specified solely by §10.8.4 H4-A/B/C**, not H3. The public announcement is ideally one clear sentence; prefer **14–16px medium/bold readable sans-serif on 390–480px mobile** and about 16px on desktop. Use a normal/wide font cut with natural letter spacing, roughly 0–0.02em (no narrow/condensed text and no excessive all-caps tracking). High text/background contrast; widen the actual text container as needed up to the safe battlefield width, rather than making the font tiny to fit a narrow 320–360px box. Aim one line for short events and **at most two legible lines** for normal actions.
- The wording should identify **real actor + card/skill + immediate verified target/result when meaningful**, in plain short English following the current game's language. Examples (only if proven by public event): "Player A played Attack on B."; "B played Dodge."; "C's Negation cancelled the Stratagem." Avoid replaying the CardFace title in a second huge heading, repeated Attack/Dodge category badges plus a long redundant explanation, and unsupported claims about damage before settlement.
- Reuse **the single already-existing public CardFace event and authoritative text**; shorten client presentation copy only, preserving event ordering, true actor/target, skill identity, private Hand privacy, all important outcome meaning and accessible chronological log. Keep existing UI-3 positioning and §8.7 4s/interruption; DO NOT add a second toast, pause the next legal response, change game rules, obscure the opponent Hero row/HP, or expand a full-screen dialog.
- Responsive positioning MUST work with H2's taller/larger opponent name and Equipment row; measure true centre CardFace and usable battlefield region, avoid clipping/overlap with side Seats, HP badges, equipment, Guidance and bottom Hand on short iPhones. If copy cannot fit in two lines, rewrite it to a SHORTER factual sentence rather than truncate a meaningful outcome. Keep full information in existing history/Inspector surfaces.

**Actual code anchors:** app/globals.css currently sizes .public-card-display-journey-copy > b at 10px (9px condensed), and app/public-card-display.tsx owns the action-specific proof-backed event copy/geometry. Fix the computed final CSS and only the proved presentational summaries; do not enlarge all HTML body text or outdated legacy panels. The Deflection framed skill/cost arrangement and already-accepted omission of its duplicate EFFECT TRIGGERED toast remain untouched.

#### 10.8.4 H4 — unified stage-fixed and stable public announcement: horizontal alignment, vertical placement, motion decoupling and no deformation (iPhone reports, 2026-10-15)

**Source of this requirement / review boundary:** The user explicitly **ACCEPTED R1 (§10.7.1)** after real iPhone testing: while a prior Attack is present, its defender can commit Dodge, the new genuine Dodge occupies the centre and the previous Attack is parked at the earlier player's actual Seat. The same user-provided screenshot (2026-10-15, approximately 10:15 UK local on iPhone Safari) reports **a separate layout defect**: the public battle announcement reading `Test Player 2 played Dodge against Test Player 3's Attack.` appears as a wide black strip shifted notably **to the RIGHT** of the large centrally revealed **Dodge** card. The parked earlier Attack thumbnail occupies the left of the battlefield, adjacent to the announcement. **Do not reopen R1 response authorization, its immediate response timing or the accepted card author-parking behavior.** This new task is **H4 announcement centering**, not R1 gameplay regression and not a request to restore central relationship arrows.

**Observed vs expected composition:** The **large authentic currently committed Dodge** and its short public explanation are **visually aligned at centre during REVEAL, while the banner is an independently positioned stage narration layer during the genuine card's MOVE/PARK lifecycle (H4-C)**. The existing design correctly puts the announcement **ABOVE** its associated real card (§10.8.3 H3), and the old Attack remains at its correct author Seat. But the message box centre must be anchored to the *actual active centre CardFace midpoint* rather than allowed to drift toward the upper-right just to avoid the parked thumbnail. On a normal 390–480px phone target **horizontal centre difference ≤12 CSS px** between announcement box and live centre CardFace; aim ≤8px. No cap on a simple always-centre design is required if justified by true safe-area/obstacle geometry, but an **80px-style drift like the provided screenshot fails**. Keep the announcement readable, not unnaturally tiny or compressed, and at most **two normal-width lines** for ordinary Attack/Dodge copy where possible.

**Source-grounded likely cause to verify, not blindly patch:** `app/public-card-display.tsx` `PublicCardAnnouncement.place()` currently enumerates candidate widths **largest first** (up to 520px), then tests shifted left offsets up to ±96px to avoid `.opponent-player-card`, `.player-square`, `[data-public-card-copy-anchor-event-id]` and other obstacles. Because large-first fitting outranks symmetry, a parked earlier Attack can induce a very wide banner **shifted right**, even though a **narrower symmetric** box or shorter factual sentence would fit above Dodge. The existing `compactMessage` option is only tried **after all original-message widths and shifts**; prefer it early when central alignment otherwise fails. There may also be stale/moving anchor geometry during Policy-B centre→Seat transitions. **Measure real DOM before choosing the fix.** `app/globals.css` sets `.public-card-display-journey-copy` positioning/text; `app/sequence-overrides.css` and `app/page.tsx` contain responsive seat/card geometry. Check final computed CSS (including mobile overrides) rather than one intermediate stylesheet declaration.

**Normative design / algorithm constraints:**
1. **Anchor to the active real CardFace:** Every per-event public announcement derives its horizontal centre from the genuine active **revealed** card's live measured rectangle. During the transition to park, use the last measured **centre-reveal** rect or the authoritative battlefield-centre fallback, **not** the moving/parked thumbnail's location. A new accepted Dodge supersedes the previous Attack as active public explanation; the announcement must follow **Dodge**, not the older Attack card, or become attached to an unrelated Seat/status.
2. **Centered candidate wins over width:** Try **centered** widths first (largest width that fits in the centered safe corridor with ≤2 lines), then switch to a **shorter factual `compactMessage`** if needed; consider a small **vertical adjustment** within genuine battlefield safe bounds rather than sliding a wide banner sideways. Selection objective should first enforce valid non-overlap, safe area and accessibility, then **minimize absolute horizontal centre offset**, then prefer readability and useful width. Do **not** retain the current width-first, 96px lateral-offset outcome when a narrower centered candidate exists. Avoid shift flicker when resizing or parked cards animate.
3. **Friendly readable copy:** The event can be summarized concisely as `Test Player 2 played Dodge vs Test Player 3.` **only when server-proven** (names, actor, target and response type). Do not remove meaning, infer damage/outcome, duplicate the card title as a giant additional banner, or change the already delivered H3 font rules. Use normal/wide ~14–16px mobile type, at most two useful lines; adapt banner width to available centre corridor. If unavoidable collisions leave no valid centered two-line location, use a verified brief plain sentence and minimum **bounded** deviation, not clipping/overlapping the top Hero row, parked Attack, side Seats, Guidance or Hand.
4. **Safe placement around real cards:** Preserve previous Attack thumbnail and true Seat/Dock history. Do **not** move the root Attack to make space, shrink the active Dodge CardFace, hide live player/HP/Equipment labels, enlarge the stage or overlay side Seats. The banner is a noninteractive status and may not intercept pointer/touch/focus; preserve the active response clock and any immediate next legal response. **During full-size REVEAL**, the announcement sits just **above** the actual central physical card with a narrow gap. **During MOVE/PARK, it stays at that independent canonical central stage band** and never follows the thumbnail; it is not docked at viewport top/right. See latest H4-C.
5. **No duplicates, wrong card binding or layout flash:** Position exactly one announcement for the newest real public event, with its own correct eventId, source and target. Test root Attack→Dodge, Attack→multiple Dodges, Duel Attack and response, Negation/counter, later root Stratagem with parked old card, and Diao Chan/Deflection public cases where different layout semantics apply. Frequent polling, reflow, iPhone Safari address-bar changes, rotated viewport, reconnect, new response interrupt and reduced-motion settings may remeasure position but must not move the banner unexpectedly to the wrong Seat or create second public text.

##### H4-B — stable central reading band across phases and counters (NEW second iPhone evidence, supersedes H4 vertical-motion ambiguity)

**User's second acceptance feedback:** In screenshot A (Steal + Negation window), the public sentence `Test Player 4 played Steal on Test Player 3; Negation can be played.` has moved up to the **bottom of the top opponent Hero row**, covering player-name/hero-seat space. In screenshot B (several genuine Negations), `Test Player 2 played Negation against Negation 3; a Negation response is open.` has moved down to **near the bottom of the battlefield**, immediately above or on preceding local parked history / status controls. The horizontal centering improvement alone from **H4-A** is INSUFFICIENT: public narration must have **one relatively stable central screen reading location through the SAME entire interaction**, rather than follow currently parked physical cards to upper/lower Seat. Treat screenshots as observations; exact layout offsets still require browser measurement before identifying the precise transition cause.

**Combined H4-A/H4-B normative geometry (one integrated repair, not two competing placement engines):**
1. Establish **one canonical, central battlefield narration corridor** using real `.play-table` geometry, actual top-row Seat/HP/name bottom, side-Seat safe edges and Local Dock/Guidance/timer top, and the **canonical full-size centre-reveal position**. Place a compact normal/wide 14–16px, 1–2 line status **horizontally centred (≤12 CSS px deviation)** within that corridor, at one **stable vertical baseline** near/just above the canonical central big-card reveal. The reading band is anchored to the **BATTLEFIELD'S central region**, not to whichever root/counter card last finished moving to an upper Hero or lower local Seat.
2. **Persist the same bounded vertical baseline across stage changes** `root reveal → root park → Negation open → Negation reveal → Negation park → next counter window` within one `interactionId/rootEventId`. On an unchanged 390–480px portrait layout target **≤16 CSS px shift in banner top between consecutive messages**, allowing text to grow upward/downward inside a reserved 2-line band without jumping the entire banner. Recalculate only for material layout/viewport change (device rotation, Safari browser toolbar/visual viewport, short landscape, seat topology), and keep it **within the safe corridor**, not near screen extremes. Do not use the previous/next moving/parked physical card's `getBoundingClientRect` directly to assign the announcement `top`.
3. **Strong safe-area bounds:** The banner must never overlap opponent Hero portrait, player name/HP, SWITCH, equipped miniatures, central active large CardFace, genuine older parked cards, shared 8s countdown, bottom local Guidance/Confirm/Pass, card Hand or view controls. If the corridor is constrained by stacked/side parked cards, prefer **shorter truthful `compactMessage`**, sensible width/line wrapping and **minor safe vertical adjustment**. Do not continuously search and settle on arbitrary far-above/far-below candidate positions simply because an older card is nearby. If a safe region genuinely disappears, use a small factual status at the nearest stable **permitted centre safe area** and record an explicit testable degraded mode (never invisibly omit an essential public event or cover another player's information).
4. **Fix real lifecycle/anchor mismatch, not CSS alone:** `PublicCardAnnouncement.place()` currently obtains an event-specific `[data-public-card-copy-anchor-event-id]` rect whenever it exists, including **move/park** phases, and a stale event can survive polling; it also collides with other genuine public cards and prefers widest original text before compact text. Check real `activeEventId`, `phase`, `fallbackCardRect`, room/interaction identity, measured stage centre, layout candidate ranking, ResizeObserver loops, iOS visualViewport and CSS `position: fixed`. Use current large centre CardFace only while actually **REVEALING** to determine shared canonical centre. Persist a stable per-interaction narration location through moving/parked responses. On a fresh independent root, reset only that interaction's baseline; do not jump because the last counter came from an upper vs lower player.
5. **Same source, one coherent status:** Keep the already proven actor, target, card and Negation/counter effect in accessible public copy without redundant long paragraphs; **never publish hidden Pass or intent identities**. User screenshot B includes language `Negation 3`; do not infer numbering from such wording for the R2-D card badge. When R2-D ordinals exist, the optionally shown public step number must agree with that exact proven sequence. Announcements have `pointer-events:none` and must not pause a new legal Negation/Pass, nor delay/shorten Policy-B 4s reveal.

**H4 integrated Coding Agent task and objective checks:** Merge original H4-A and this H4-B into ONE small presentational fix; do not implement an H4-A-only patch that still jumps to the viewport top/bottom. Build an authenticated Worker/D1 **four-viewer** test with **one Steal root + four committed Negations, including two from the same actor**. Capture one common true `interactionId`, each `eventId`, `data-public-card-announcement-event-id`, card `data-public-card-journey-phase`, announcement `DOMRect`, canonical battlefield safe corridor and current prior-card Seat rect every phase from root to final. Assert on stable 390×844 and 440×894 (plus 390×700, 480×900 and 4/6/8 seat layouts): **≤12px horizontal centre error** and **≤16px successive top movement** under unchanged geometry; **zero overlap** with top Hero/HP/name bars, protected cards, timer, Local Dock/Hand and current active central real CardFace; no fallback placement outside the safe centre corridor; at most two readable lines for normal concise battle copy. Test root Attack→Dodge, multi-Negation, Duel/Deflection, source at top/left/right/local, multiple polls, new independent root reset, long player names, Safari toolbar shift, reconnect and reduced motion. Prefer a **single measured fixed corridor + persistent per-interaction anchor** over a multi-branch CSS patch. Deliver real screenshot/DOM geometry proof, focused client/browser/API regressions and exact-SHA normal pipeline; mark **H4 PENDING REVIEW** only. **R1 and original R2-A/B/C are already USER-ACCEPTED** and must not be reopened; H4 is NEW undelivered UX work.


##### H4-C — decouple narration from physical card movement; reserve a non-deforming central text band (NEW H3 phone-review evidence, 2026-10-15)

**Latest user acceptance boundary:** On real iPhone the user CONFIRMED **H3's normal/wide typography, concise factual wording and legibility ARE ACCEPTED** while the card is large. They separately report that **during the physical CardFace shrink/translation to the actual player's Hero Seat/Dock, the public announcement MOVES WITH the card**, producing visibly poor animation. When the active root / current card and text already sit toward the top of the battlefield, existing top-row opponent Hero cards or parked physical CardFaces intrude, **squeezing/distorting the announcement box**. These are **H4 dynamic placement defects**, NOT grounds to reopen H3's accepted typography, gameplay, legitimate 4-second Policy-B reveal, or true-owner card parking. **Implement H4-A/H4-B/H4-C together as ONE shared public-announcement layout fix; no separate competing systems.**

**Definitive unified lifecycle (overrides any earlier phrase implying narration must follow a card's actual changing rect):**

1. **Card and text are independent layers after event association:** While a real card is in its full-size centre **REVEAL**, the public information appears **above that genuine large CardFace**, horizontally centered and readable. The **event ID/actor/target/text remain linked to the proven card**, but the banner's **CSS position/transform is not a child of, and must not be bound frame-by-frame to, that CardFace's shrink/move animation**. At the beginning of the move to owner Seat, the card alone animates. The public banner **remains in the canonical centre reading band**—no flying/sliding/shrinking toward the actor, no transform/scale inheritance, no per-frame `getBoundingClientRect()` following the moving thumbnail. If a newer genuine committed response appears, the **text can cross-fade/change IN PLACE** to the new event, never travel from old author seat to new author seat.
2. **One stable reserved narration corridor, derived from the actual battlefield:** Compute the usable safe band between the bottom of top-row opponent Seats (Hero name/HP/SWITCH/Equipment and any real owner-parked card history) and the upper edge of bottom/local Hand/Guidance/Confirm/Pass/timer, respecting side Seats, true centre CardFace and safe viewport bounds. Give the public announcement a **stable max width and sufficient intrinsic 1–2 line height**, with predictable padding/line-height and a safe top baseline. The natural banner width should remain visually consistent for successive short events; do not dynamically compress the banner into a narrow, tall, squashed strip to fit between another player's thumbnails, and do not shrink its accepted H3 font. Prefer **shortening proven prose** over changing physical typography or allowing 3+ cramped lines. When a layout actually changes, recompute the one corridor coherently, not in reaction to individual card animations.
3. **Top-seat collision has highest priority:** Opponent top-row Hero cards, HP, SWITCH, name/equipment bands and **their parked card miniatures** are protected obstacles, not alternative announcement anchors. The common narration baseline belongs **below** those real top-zone elements and **above** the central card, with an explicit readable gap. Never overlay top hero/Equipment/name cards, push information to the very top, move it to the very bottom, or **warp its width/height** to escape obstacles. If the exact two-line band cannot fit above the canonical large card on a short viewport, use an explicitly tested **nearby fixed battlefield centre sub-region** and compact truthful wording; resolve exceptional space constraints without recreating arbitrary per-event top/bottom bouncing or covering active controls. Preserve the true card's centre-to-Seat motion/size.
4. **Stable proof-linked message with calm updates:** In a single root/Negation/counter, Hold/Reveal → Move → Park → next response window can change the message content and truthfully report the latest event, but **the banner's own horizontal centre remains within ≤12 CSS px of the canonical central reveal centre** and **its top changes ≤16 CSS px across unchanged viewport/Seat geometry**. The announcement should not flicker, vanish, duplicate, squeeze or jump when its tracked event ID changes from root to counter or React remounts/polls. Use stable component/band identity for a common interaction even as the `eventId` changes. A genuinely new root may change factual text and scope ID but should reuse the same layout corridor at an unchanged seat topology.
5. **The existing text/rules are accepted:** Preserve H3 normal/wide ≈14–16px high-contrast type, plain concise actor/card/target wording, 1–2 normal lines, no extra headers/duplicate popups, verified public identity only, no response-blocking pointer events. Keep server game logic, public proof and private simultaneous Negation intents unchanged. Do **not** hide or materially abbreviate meaningful public outcome to meet visual geometry; use the existing accessible history for richer detail as specified by H3.

**Coding Agent single combined H4 delivery checklist (H4-A/B/C):**

- **Objective automated + human-readable evidence:** Test 390×844, 390×700, 440×894, 480×900 (and desktop), top-row 4/6/8/10 with side Seats where topology supports; hero/name/HP/equipment and old parked Attack/Negation physically present. While genuine CardFace goes from full-size centre → moving → parked under its author, assert **banner movement ≤16px vertically** and **horizontal centroid deviation ≤12px** relative to the **canonical centre** under unchanged geometry, **no inherited card transform**, 1–2 readable lines, no forced condensed fontsize/squeezed banner, **zero intersections with top-row Hero/HP/Equipment/parked physical cards**, current large CardFace, local Hand/decision area or timer. ##### W3-F2-R1 — unified shared announcement stability amendment (LATEST NORMATIVE SCOPE; owner requested 2026-10-24 23:36 UTC)

**Supersedes the per-card branch-limited approach in R1.3 above, WITHOUT changing this original task ID.** The owner requested that Planner examine *all situations that could flicker* and design one reusable fix instead of separate Hua Tuo, Steal and Burning Bridges hotfixes. One coordinated implementation may use ordered internal commits but shall have **one combined production verification / owner iPhone re-review**, not independent, falsely accepted per-card microtasks.

**Evidence-grade inventory: what is proven and what is an audit target.**
- **CONFIRMED on owner iPhone / trace:** (A) Hua Tuo Prodigal Healer public COST earlier kept a stale message across turn/Attack and flashed (initial trace: 52 visibility transitions / 56 readiness flips in ~1.9s); (B) first repaired build `3eec03d` still visibly flashes in **Steal** and **Burning Bridges** during TEST SWITCH in 4-player Negation and/or physical `target_card` choice, and stops once the target-card choice/transfer/discard settles. It has NO full per-frame announcement-visibility record. Distinguish these user failures from risk across untested paths.
- **CONFIRMED shared code entry inventory (current `ux-v2`):** `app/public-card-display.tsx PublicCardAnnouncement` is already reused by (1) `SingleTargetCardJourney` (`single-target`, `negation`, `group-root`, `lust-cost`), (2) `AttackDodgeCardJourney`, (3) `DuelCardJourney` (`duel`, `lust-duel`), (4) fallback static `PublicCardDisplay`, and (5) `PublicSkillEventAnnouncementLayer`. It is **not** correct to treat all five as the same physical-card animator; each owns its own genuine card transitions, but all need ONE reusable banner lifetime/anchor policy. `app/page.tsx` separately renders legacy `TableResolutionSequence`, `effect-notice`, `turn-notice`, `PublicActivityChip`, private-draw and decision UI: audit duplicated **public root** ownership and collisions without collapsing intentional independent private/current-action guidance. `effect-notice` and H4's accepted public copy are *protected* independent scope unless actual duplicate/flashing proof identifies a shared boundary defect.

Existing common placer sets `copy.style.visibility="hidden"` when `displayedCopy` differs or geometry is pending/anchor unavailable, and `"visible"` after each success; `useLayoutEffect` dependencies include mutable copy, narration and layout fields, allowing repeated measurement/restarts. `lastValidPlacementRef` cache is keyed by `announcementIdentity` that currently combines **viewer layout AND changing message/checkpoint text**, which can unnecessarily invalidate safe geometric reuse for one public root. `onJourneyOwnershipChange` in `SingleTargetCardJourney` and `reportPublicCardJourneyOwnership` in `app/page.tsx` are another potential viewer-switch feedback path. These are **CODE-SUPPORTED potential shared flicker mechanisms**; exactly which fires per untested card route remains UNKNOWN until tracing.

**Architecture / implementation contract: share the banner engine, do NOT replace all existing card renderers.**
**U1 — One pure, proof-gated public announcement arbiter.** In `app/page.tsx` or a small pure extracted helper, derive one *active public announcement snapshot* from current server-committed event facts, not last React render. Define typed stable semantic identity at least `(roomCode, rootEventId, committed checkpoint/response eventId, presentationRevision when genuinely changed, public actorId, action class)`; keep `viewerId` out of the **event identity** but use it when choosing privacy-filtered visible words. Enforce one eligible current shared public banner per root/window; deterministic precedence for current committed response/Negation/settlement and legitimate held read versus older Hero COST/static/history. Uncommitted client selection, queued expired effects, mere timeline presence, TEST SWITCH or layout observer work must NOT elect a new public event or restart its read. Terminate or supersede completed root copy after genuine public reading, while preserving PARKED genuine card history and an *ongoing server-owned* response window. A later confirmed event preempts old copy promptly and atomically, including changes to source/target/result. Fail closed on missing public proof or mismatch and preserve all private owner Hand/role filtering.
**U2 — Semantic ownership state machine shared across view modes.** Reuse/centralize the existing `SingleTargetCardJourney` idempotent ownership record as a small typed hook/pure helper (for example `usePublicAnnouncementOwnership` / `selectPublicAnnouncementOwnership`), keyed by stable room/root/action/event/card proof IDs, with explicit `UNSEEN -> ACTIVE -> READING -> RETIRED` **copy** stages while `REVEAL -> MOVE -> PARKED` remains the separate **physical-card** state. Do **not** let a copied message own a real physical card or let a parked card resurrect an active banner. Explicitly distinguish active semantic event authority from *per-viewer* layout availability. Viewer switch must produce a new layout epoch/geometry without revoking root ownership to legacy `TableResolutionSequence`; only a real room/root/action retirement, unmount or proof change may release it. Parent and child callbacks must be idempotent by semantic sets, fenced with generation/scope to reject stale cleanup; no true/false ping-pong from same-event re-renders, polling, `journey.cards` reference changes or pending geometry. Keep `PublicCardDisplay` single renderer owning each genuine event/card; duplicate hidden legacy copy/physical CardFace must remain suppressed even while the new viewer measures.
**U3 — One reusable stable announcement placement engine for ALL `PublicCardAnnouncement` callers.** Refactor the existing `PublicCardAnnouncement` into an internal stable placement hook/helper (`useStablePublicAnnouncementPlacement` or equivalent) **used unconditionally** by its five existing callers. Remove the Hua-Tuo-only opt-in `stableCopyPlacement` gating; no `cardKind`-specific boolean flags, hard-coded Steal/Burning Bridges band coordinates, or parallel one-off placement loops. Define two different keys: `eventCopyKey` = committed public root + current semantic checkpoint (for text/aria update) and `geometryKey` = current viewerId + layout revision/viewport/table/seat-geometry epoch (for safe screen rect). A same-root genuine checkpoint update changes text/aria and may resize the banner **without unmounting or hiding/reappearing solely because wording changed**; place within the accepted central-safe anchor corridor, using latest valid geometry for this same viewer. A genuine viewer/viewport/Seat change invalidates old-viewer rect immediately; measure new anchors and commit text+position atomically before visible paint, or if geometry is temporarily unsafe allow **at most one deliberate hidden interval per real switch** until safe, never old-viewer misplacement. Never keep a stale cached rect after the viewport/Seat layout materially changes or reuse private-viewer text.
**U4 — Read/write isolation to prevent observer/React feedback loops.** Keep the current collision/protected rect checks (Seat, Dock, Hand, response timer, Inspector, private draw, Harvest pool, safe-zone), but on a stable event/viewer do not rewrite DOM style/attributes or fire React state updates when semantic copy+rect is equal within 1 CSS px. Batch only real geometry reads and safe writes in one `requestAnimationFrame` transaction; de-duplicate `ResizeObserver`/`MutationObserver` triggers and do not listen to self-generated `visibility/style/dataset/aria-live` changes that cause another reflow cycle. Use monotonic layout generation to fence stale timer/RAF after event/viewer changes; avoid restarting `useLayoutEffect`/setting hidden on unrelated `displayedCopy` changes. If frame collision blocks every legal position, keep at most one last-known-safe rect for **same viewer/layout** for a bounded geometric recheck; after sustained unsafe geometry hide **once**, trace exact obstacle, and restore **once** when a safe layout exists, never blink repeatedly. Do not use arbitrary global delays or `visibility:visible!important` to conceal faults.
**U5 — Unify banner copy lifecycle across all five callers, without flattening card-specific history.** Pass the same stable semantic `eventCopyKey`, `geometryKey`, proof-based active status, public actor and allowed `aria-live` text to the common banner from `SingleTargetCardJourney`, `AttackDodgeCardJourney`, `DuelCardJourney`, fallback static `PublicCardDisplay` and `PublicSkillEventAnnouncementLayer`. Preserve case-specific card paths, true Hand discard/Steal transfer/Burning Bridges discard, Duel ordinals, Negation chronology, Group/AOE, Harvest pool, W3/W4 Hero COST and First Aid conversion; no generic rebuilding of physical CardFaces. For `effect-notice`, H4 and `PublicActivityChip`, audit precedence and card-root identity: leave legitimately separate guidance visible as currently accepted, but a **second notice for the same public root** must not fight over status/ARIA or flip the shared banner on and off. Continue one appropriate user-facing public `role=status` per active public proof event; screen-reader text changes only on committed semantic checkpoints, never on render/observer frames. Do not rewrite unrelated local decision messages, timers or turn notices to this module.
**U6 — One delivery boundary with small deterministic steps.** Agent may use internal commit (A) standalone pure arbiter and ownership equality helper + unit tests, (B) common placement hook + adapt all five callers, (C) cross-renderer/duplicate-notice guards and focused authentic Worker/D1 smoke; integrate/CI/deploy as **one complete W3-F2-R1 repair**, never release only an opt-in `if Steal` patch and call overall solved. #### 10.9.1 Normative Frame grammar and lifecycle

| Class | One framed centre composition (top to bottom) | Meaning / examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A — COST** | **Real Hero skill / Equipment name** → **every actually paid real physical CardFace** (one, exactly two or all selected) → optionally concise cost/outcome cue | Discard/spend genuine Hand or Equipment material to activate a skill. Example: Deflection, Betrothment, Rock Cleaving Axe. These cards are **costs, NOT individually played Attack/Dodge**. |
| **C — CONVERSION** | **Real skill / Equipment name** → **source physical CardFace(s)** → compact explicit **AS ATTACK / AS DODGE / AS PEACH / AS BURNING BRIDGES / AS OVERINDULGENCE** | A genuine card or two-card bundle is used **as another semantic card**. Original picture, kind, rank, suit and exact physical IDs remain visible; do not draw a fabricated second virtual card. Example: Braveheart, Serpent Spear. |
| **E — EFFECT / JUDGEMENT** | **True Equipment / skill name** → **only real, already-public affected/committed CardFace(s), when any exist** → truthful, short result | An actual further Attack, a revealed Judgement, forced discard of another character's cards, or other physical event. If no publicly authorized physical card exists, use **short nonblocking text**, not a blank/fake Frame. Example: Eight Trigrams, Green Dragon Blade, Kirin Bow. |

- **One frame, no duplicate toast:** Preserve the same subtle framed style as accepted §10.5.3, name ABOVE material cards, compact single true explanation in the existing public-card narration. When a dedicated proof-backed frame fully describes an activation, suppress only the duplicate generic EFFECT TRIGGERED notice for that **same event ID**; do not suppress unrelated Hero/Equipment notices. No floating second skill badge below card, no separate giant skill/relationship panel, no green/red connectors.
- **Card counts:** one CardFace is centred, two CardFaces appear side-by-side inside the same frame; three or more use a responsive compact strip/grid/contained scroll with all real cards inspectable and the true count visible. Divine Wisdom/Equilibrium can spend many cards: never crop away inaccessible paid identities, invent omitted cards, overflow the battlefield, or add an unrelated second presentation. Small screens may scale authentic CardFaces consistently, with an accessible complete cost list and one active focal group; preserve legible corners where practical.
- **Committed-only:** Private selection, unconfirmed trigger, declined/cancelled/expired/stale action, pending Negation intent, unrevealed Hand and speculative play **must never create a public CardFace or reveal card IDs**. Reveal only the exact card(s) that the server has committed as *publicly identifiable* according to the game's actual event/rules. For a hidden/random Hand discard lacking an authoritative public reveal, display a truthful public quantity/anonymous back only if even that fact is public; do **not** upgrade a logged private card ID to a public face merely to fill the frame.
- **Event linkage:** Each frame needs a server-verifiable semantic skill/equipment ID, activating actor, actual cost/affected-card owner(s), exact committed physical IDs, public event ID(s), root interaction/resolution/frame linkage when relevant, and played-as/outcome status. Existing **PROVEN** Deflection proof is specific to redirect and **must not be copied or asserted for other abilities without genuine checks**. Fail closed to a short accurate public notice if the relevant event proof is missing; do not guess from nearby log messages, current Hand, equipped weapon, HP loss or visual timing.
- **Movement and ownership:** Author-attached public action history follows real actor Seat/Dock (§8), but the *physical discarded card owner* may differ from the skill activator. Distinguish **activationOwnerId**, **materialOwnerId**, **physicalCardId**, target and actual zone transition. Centre frame names the actual trigger owner; a cost belongs to its real payer. For target-forced discard, material parks/retire at the **target's** true Seat/zone, not the weapon holder's; a pre-existing Attack remains at its original author. Preserve one card ID / one visual owner / one actual Hand–Equipment–Discard–Judgement state and correct final history.
- **Policy B:** The committed group receives the normal §8.7 up-to-4s central reveal and ~380ms park, interrupted promptly only by a newer genuine, authoritative, committed public response. Visual staging never blocks legal CurrentAction responses, Dodge, Negation, Dying/Peach, target selection, timer or the touchable local Hand. Multiple fast events follow real commit sequence; stale polls, refresh, reconnect, test-viewer switch and reduced motion cannot duplicate, reassign, hide or mis-order cards.
- **Conversion semantics:** The centre always shows the **original** real card(s), plus AS semantic outcome, **never replaces its art with a fake transformed card**. The server alone owns effective Attack/Dodge/Peach/Stratagem legality and effects; use its actual origin, playedAs and response proof. If a transformed card becomes a delayed card in a **Judgement zone** (Da Qiao Captivating), honour that authoritative final zone and Negation lifecycle rather than falsely parking it forever as discarded.
- **Language/layout:** Canonical English printed skill/equipment labels are authoritative; the optionally displayed Chinese skill name is supplemental. Avoid duplicating source card title as an extra heading. Frame does not overlap battlefield/Seats/side Seats/Hand/Guidance/timer at 390×844, 440×894, 480×900 and short 390×700; test 4/6/8/10-seat geometry, accessible captions and hit targets. For any battle announcement reuse §10.8 H3 normal/wide readable text above the physical group, without an additional explanatory banner.

### 10.10 Shared public target-card selection and outcome for Steal / Burning Bridges — newly approved multiplayer UX correction (2026-10-15)

**User-observed defect:** When a player uses **Steal (顺手牵羊)** or **Burning Bridges / Dismantle (过河拆桥)**, the operating player can see their private target-card chooser and the card taking/discarding effect, but **other participants cannot understand what is occurring**. Fix the **shared public journey on every authenticated viewer screen**, without showing private Hand cards or private live picker choices. This task is **new public-progress/outcome UX**, **not** a request to reimplement the already delivered centre/park ROOT Stratagem (§10.2.B) or change these cards' game rules. It overrides any earlier §10.2 source-review **NO CHANGE** classification as to the newly reported observer visual gap only.

**Source-grounded baseline from current `ux-v2` inspection:** `app/api/rooms/route.ts` already publicly projects `pendingTargetCard` containing the action's `kind`, `sourceId`, `actorId` and `targetId` after Negation settles; `CurrentAction.targetCardSelection` is the **actor-only** authoritative eligible-key picker. The actor's `app/page.tsx` `TargetCardPicker` correctly shows anonymous `hand:n` positions and genuinely public Equipment/Judgement candidates, but no equivalent small observer progress surface is presently driven from `pendingTargetCard`. The existing server emits proof-backed `publicDismantleSettlement` on a genuine discard CardFace, and `publicStealSettlement` on a generic settlement **message** that intentionally omits the taken card's identity. The validated `game/presentation-v2.ts` and `game/presentation-snapshot.ts` projections therefore establish ROOT/settlement identity but do **not currently express the complete public origin-zone/movement narrative**. `app/page.tsx` has settlement candidates for both and supplies their original root `cardFace` to `PublicCardDisplay`; the new work should **extend** this rather than mount an unrelated duplicate presenter. This is a targeted source-inspection finding, **not** a claim that the full remote UI was reproduced on real phones in this review.

#### 10.10.1 Non-negotiable everyone-can-follow sequence

| Stage | Actor-only interaction | Public state visible to every other player |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Committed root** | Original physical Steal/Burning Bridges card is accepted and uses existing §8.7 centre→true actor Seat/Dock Policy-B journey | Everyone sees same genuine root card, real source and targeted player. Preserve applicable **§9 private all-seat Negation** before the effect; no target card is available for selection during an unresolved/cancelled Negation window. |
| **2. Authoritative choosing** | Only authorized actor sees the existing clickable black/gold Hand/Equipment/Judgement `TargetCardPicker`, with anonymous target Hand positions | All other viewers see a **small, nonblocking, publicly truthful indicator** near the target Seat or just above the existing root journey: `A is choosing one card from B…` plus the real card-effect name. Show real source and target with a gentle progress affordance. Do **not** copy the interactive picker, reveal which zone/card/position is under the pointer, identify Hand cards, or publish selection/revision/hover/tap events. The status persists across polls and reconnect while the server's target-card pending state is active. |
| **3A. Committed Steal settlement** | Server removes **exactly one** real card from target Hand/Equipment/Judgement and adds it to the actor's **private Hand** | All viewers see the source→target connection through text and a **single target-origin→actor-destination visual move** or compact zone-attached transition. If taken from hidden Hand, move an **anonymous face-down back** only; no art/name/suit/rank/cardId/hand position or private future Hand contents. Show proven public Hand counts updating. If taken from a **public Equipment or Judgement zone**, the exact previously public CardFace may be shown **only when a genuine typed public removal/transfer proof identifies it**; remove it from target's displayed zone and briefly show its movement to actor's Hand without leaving a permanent face-up "played" card or exposing later private Hand state. Text: `A stole one card from B's Hand/Equipment/Judgement` only if that zone is server-proven; otherwise `A stole one card from B`. |
| **3B. Committed Burning Bridges settlement** | Server removes **exactly one** genuine card from target Hand/Equipment/Judgement and places it in actual Discard | All viewers see the target-zone→**non-visible Discard anchor** transition and a short authentic `A discarded one card from B's [proven zone]` result. The current server's public `discard` CardFace event can support the original real physical art **after authoritative commitment** when game rules/public projection permit revealing that discarded card; no identity is exposed **while selecting**. Public Equipment/Judgement selections use their already-public identity. If the card's identity is not authorized for a specific case, use a back/quantity notice instead, not a guessed face. Never resurrect the permanently visible Deck/Discard piles forbidden by §8.2. |
| **4. Settlement/retirement** | Correct source and target zones/Hand state updated | Every viewer sees one coherent completion cue with exact card owner/result; no merely cryptic `STEAL RESOLVED` / `BURNING BRIDGE RESOLVED` without explaining who gained/discarded from whom. Original root parks/retains true author's public history as §8/§10.7 requires, while the taken/discarded card never falsely parks as a played Stratagem at the wrong Seat. Retire transient progress/motion after settlement; preserve accessible chronological public history. |

**Important before/after privacy boundary:** It is public that **A is acting on B**; it is **not public** which hidden card, hidden Hand index, currently hovered target, or even which eligible zone A is considering before confirmation. Even if a chosen source zone becomes publicly provable after server commit, **never extrapolate an opponent's remaining Hand identities**. A face-up Equipment/Judgement card was already public; moving it into a Hand does not grant perpetual inspection into that Hand. Do not expose `CurrentAction`, private target-selection keys, secret Negation provider/Pass state, or session tokens to other viewers.

**Two different physical outcomes, not one generic movement:** Steal physically TRANSFERS a card to the actor's Hand; Dismantle physically DISCARDS it. Destination, count changes, animation lifetime and log wording must correspond exactly. A stored real CardFace can never simultaneously appear as an Equipment miniature, a moving public card and a permanently "played" card; transient animation ownership must not duplicate the live server card zone. Do not transform the *root Steal/Burning Bridges card* into the selected/removed target card or create a second imaginary root.

#### 10.10.2 One shared observer UX, no rule changes or double presentation

- **Source of truth:** Public choosing state must derive from the authenticated server's `pendingTargetCard` (or the equivalent proven public semantic projection), not from `room.isMyAction`, local modal open, a stale cached `CurrentAction`, or guesses from `room.actionPlayerId`. All clients (actor, victim and unaffected seats) use the same committed root/action/settlement IDs; only the genuine actor receives editable picker selections.
- **Proof extension for animated zone transitions:** Inspect and minimally extend the authoritative Steal/Dismantle settlement payload to carry a **publicly safe** `sourceZone` (`hand|equipment|judgement`) and **actual affected-card owner/source/target**. For *public* Equipment/Judgement movement, include the exact genuine public CardFace/card ID with necessary causal/root/event linkage; for **hidden-Hand Steal**, NEVER expose actual card identity, `hand:n` index or private IDs in public JSON, timeline, snapshot, DOM, attributes, accessible text, debug or presentation telemetry. A typed public opaque **movement-event ID** may drive the one anonymous back. Do not rely on client diffing zone arrays/Hand counts or guessing the movement's cause. When proof is unavailable, show the factual quantity/result without an invented physical animation.
- **Discard identity policy:** The current Dismantle server emits one public `discard` CardFace; before reusing this for target-Hand discards, confirm its public identity semantics against the project rules. The new UX must never increase disclosure relative to authoritative allowed public events. If the rules differ by origin zone, encode that server-side and test all viewers' **raw wire JSON**, not just screen text.
- **Existing presenter first:** Reuse the root public card journey, short H3-readable public sentence, Seat/Dock/hidden-discard animation anchors and `publicDismantleSettlement`/`publicStealSettlement` projections. The public status is a **compact seat-related phase label**, not a giant card-selection dialog, a relationship graph/arrow, a permanent overlaid deck/discard or a second simultaneous large central CardFace. Ensure the affected-card motion does not violate §8.7: **only a newer committed public response/counter CardFace** interrupts an existing Policy-B centre reveal, and a target-card private selection or mere settlement is NOT such a response. New physical disposition may animate locally without stealing root centre or blocking controls.
- **Obsolete/cancelled:** Cancelled/Negated Steal or Burning Bridges shows its real Negation outcome and **no** choosing/transfer/discard animation; invalid/stale/double submissions never produce ghost effects. If source/target dies, Equipment is replaced, selected Hand index moves, a new independent root starts or a prior public interaction retires, follow actual server settlement/cleanup; do not show a former pending status indefinitely. Preserve causal fix R2.
- **Performance:** Public phase cue must be readable for non-actor viewers who did not open the picker; don't allow a one-poll flash to hide the only transfer result. Use server event IDs for replay/dedup and reasonable bounded read time, without artificially extending the current turn or locking a new legal response. Never emit user-specific interactive selection to a spectator.

**CONFIRMED SOURCE DEFECTS (references identify the actual implementation rather than guessing from appearance):**

1. **Steal settlement discards its renderer/motion contract.** In `app/page.tsx`, `singleTargetNegationPublicAction` and the normal proved `rootAction.cardKind === "Steal" || "Dismantle"` branch both construct `motion: { type: "single-target", scopeKey: [room.code, rootEventId].join(":"), freshEventIds }`. The `dismantleSettlementCandidate` branch preserves that contract. **The adjacent `stealSettlementCandidate` branch builds a new action with card/source/settlement but NO `motion` at all.** In `app/public-card-display.tsx PublicCardDisplay()`, absence of this motion bypasses `SingleTargetCardJourney` and selects the centrally positioned `static-fallback` renderer. React cannot preserve the same moving card element/phase across this component-type switch. This is an actionable defect even if its precise appearance depends on which branch wins the current action priority.

2. **Movement is forcibly completed by ordinary layout work.** `app/public-card-display.tsx SingleTargetCardJourney()` has a layout `reflow()` scheduled by `ResizeObserver`, `MutationObserver` and window/`visualViewport` resize. Its initial state update sets `suppressTransitions: true`, `layoutPending: true`, and **turns every current `phase === "move"` card into `phase: "parked", rect: card.target, moveStartedAtMs: null`**; the subsequent measurement uses `const phase = card.phase === "move" ? "parked" : card.phase` and also sets `suppressTransitions: true`. In `app/globals.css`, `.public-card-display-journey.is-reflowing .public-card-journey-card.is-parked` disables transitions. Thus an unrelated or unchanged-size layout observer callback can complete an intended ~380ms move instantaneously. The reveal timer otherwise correctly starts `move` after the ~4000ms hold when geometry is known and reduced motion is off; the ordinary move timer correctly expires after `MOVE_DURATION_MS = 380`. **Fix the reflow override, not those accepted durations.**

3. **Freshness and ownership can change when the presentation action changes.** `app/page.tsx` prioritizes the held Negation action, live single-target root and Steal/Dismantle settlement action in `livePublicCardAction` / `selectedPublicCardAction`; their current `action.key` strings differ even for the same `rootEventId`. `SingleTargetCardJourney` uses `motion.scopeKey` for its state but also reports `action.key` in `onJourneyOwnershipChange`. `app/page.tsx publicCardJourneySeenEventIds` normally records an event after it is parked, not during reveal/move. A transient no-motion/no-action transition may unmount the journey while the root remains unmarked fresh; a subsequent re-mounted journey can treat the **same** proved root as fresh again. In parallel, `publicDisplayOwnedEventIds` / `publicDisplayOwnedPhysicalCardIds` filter `TableResolutionSequence` only while the public-card renderer claims presentation. The implementation has no single uninterrupted root-owner guarantee across these action branches. **This is a CONFIRMED lifecycle/ownership gap with a plausible duplicate-centre path; the precise branch transition must be proved by the Agent's controlled browser test before claiming it alone accounts for every observed movement.**

4. **Local-author anchor ambiguity remains independent of the two defects above.** `app/public-card-display.tsx seatHistoryCardParking()` and fallback `actorParkedCard()` currently select the first visible `[data-player-anchor]` matching `actorId`; only an explicit `anchorLocalHero` option prefers `.local-player-dock`, currently used by another presentation family. This is a **source-confirmed unsafe selection policy**, not proof that the particular failure required a duplicate anchor. Fix anchor authority with a narrow, identity-based rule without moving any actual Seat or Dock.

### 10.11 Stargazing whole-card touch drag — NEW user-reported iPhone usability fix, 2026-10-15

**User's observed problem:** Zhuge Liang's **Stargazing (观星)** currently feels as if cards can be rearranged only by tapping `Move / Top / Bottom / Earlier / Later` buttons. **Required visible interaction:** directly **touch-and-hold anywhere on the genuine CardFace, then drag the physical card** to either deck zone or a new position in its current zone; menu buttons remain as a secondary accessible alternative. This is a usability/regression task for the **existing PRIVATE deck-reorder dialog (§5.2)**, not a new Hero rules feature and **NOT** a §10.9 public skill-cost Frame. Do not put the private Stargazing faces in public centre/seat animation.

**Source inspection — existing implementation is PARTIAL, do not reimplement blindly:** `app/page.tsx` `PrivateDeckReorderDialog` already has `DeckDrag`, pointer capture, a 260ms touch hold, insertion markers, top/unassigned/bottom arrangements, edge auto-scroll, keyboard/screen-reader Move menu and the authoritative `private_deck_reorder` submit. However `beginDrag()` explicitly **returns for touch unless the original touched element is inside `[data-deck-touch-handle]`**. The touch handle is `.deck-reorder-drag-grip` in `app/sequence-overrides.css`, only **27×27 CSS px** at the card corner with `touch-action: none`; the rest of `.deck-reorder-card-face` uses `touch-action: pan-x pan-y` and is not a touch drag origin. Thus the code currently **does not support ordinary whole-card long-press drag** even though §5.2 had described generalized touch-hold dragging. This identifies a **specific source-supported UX gap**, not independent real-device reproduction; perform a live device/browser test before claiming repaired.

#### 10.11.1 Exact gesture contract

1. **Whole-card gesture, 1/2/N cards:** On the authorized actor's private Stargazing dialog, a finger placed on **any non-control point within the displayed actual physical CardFace**, including the art, title or lower edge, is a valid touch source. A short deliberate long-press (approximately 200–300ms; calibrate to reliable iOS Safari behavior) **visibly picks up that card** with a lifted/dragging treatment. The user can then move it freely without releasing; releasing over a valid zone commits the local rearrangement. Pointer/mouse on desktop may press-and-drag directly without a long hold. The tiny optional grip must **not** be a prerequisite; it may remain as a visual affordance but should not consume a large portion of a 64–94px card.
2. **Three genuine interactive zones, not just buttons:** From any of **REVEALED CARDS (unassigned)**, **TOP OF DECK**, **BOTTOM OF DECK**, the dragged card can be dropped into either other zone or repositioned **before, between or after** cards in its current zone. Empty top/bottom rows accept drops across a comfortable whole-row hit area. Highlight the actual target zone and show a stable, visible insertion caret/gap before release; the lifted card follows the finger without obstructing the drop hit test. The three rows remain in the same vertical order as §5.2.
3. **Ordering is semantically important:** TOP left→right = first actual future draw to later draws; BOTTOM left→right = the existing server-required bottom order after the remaining deck. Verify the actual `topCardIds` and `bottomCardIds` arrays after moves: inserting ahead of another card must preserve the exact visual order, not reverse it or shift by an off-by-one error when dragging within one row. Drop into another row removes the original position. Each original card ID exists in exactly one of `unassigned / top / bottom` throughout every action.
4. **Cancellation and scroll behavior:** Native page/contained-row scrolling and intended vertical dialog scroll should not accidentally begin a drag on a quick tap/swipe. Once an explicit hold has activated drag, prevent competing native pan/context menu/text selection so iOS does not cancel or steal the pointer; allow the user to reach off-screen positions by edge auto-scroll. Before activation, a quick swipe to scroll should behave normally where practical; scroll gestures should **not** move a card. A `pointercancel`, Escape, drag outside valid zones, panel disappearance, server action-revision change, lost capture, multi-finger interference or stale submission leaves the exact previous arrangement and does not leak a card to another zone. Account for CSS `touch-action` and pointer capture on the **whole CardFace**, not only grip, without breaking vertical scrolling or the Move menu.
5. **Honest feedback and accessibility:** Show a readable short instruction `Hold and drag a card to Top or Bottom; drag again to change order`. Active card visibly lifts; target zone / insertion point shows contrast and non-color cue, with a succinct live confirmation of its resulting zone and 1-based position. Preserve real card art, rank and suit in this *private* dialog only. Keep the `Move` menu and Earlier/Later/Top/Bottom/Return accessible for keyboard, screen-reader and users unable to drag; `COMPLETE STARGAZING` remains reachable without dragging. Focus return/announcement and `prefers-reduced-motion` are respected.
6. **Server, privacy and completion unchanged:** No mutation or requests on drag; submit only once the user clicks **COMPLETE STARGAZING** using existing `{providerId:"private_deck_reorder",topCardIds,bottomCardIds}` contract and server-projected `minTop/maxTop`. Completion disabled while any card remains unassigned, constraints fail or an action is busy/stale. All-to-Top / all-to-Bottom are valid only if the authoritative constraint allows. **All true card identities remain private to Zhuge Liang's viewer**: other clients, spectator/debug presentation, timeline, DOM/ARIA outside the owner dialog and server public events never learn the four drawn/private revealed cards or local drag positions.
7. **Responsive minimum:** At 390×844 and short 390×700 iPhone viewport, a card remains easily touch-holdable and moving between vertically separated zones never clips off-screen or drops onto action buttons. Also test 360/440/480px phone and different number of revealed cards (including five when server affords). Validation is mobile-only per the product owner's instruction; do not require desktop visual/pointer checks. Preserve §5.2 four-card recognizability, horizontal contained scrolling when necessary, safe-area insets, sticky/accessible submit, full control reachability and no overscroll of main game Hand/Seats.

### 10.12 UI-4-F — Diao Chan Lust: public activity chip, local guidance, single cost Frame and generated-Duel history (user iPhone feedback, 2026-10-15)

**Review verdict:** §10.6 UI-4 original technical delivery was green but **NOT USER ACCEPTED for Lust**. Five real iPhone screenshots show: (1) Local Dock Guidance wastes room on \`YOUR DECISION\`, \`Test Player 2's turn\` and \`LOCAL CANCEL / Change your selection\`, plus a Cancel button; important \`Lust order\` is squeezed BELOW the main guidance box. (2) The true paid **5♣ Hex Mark** appears alone at battlefield centre while \`LUST\` and player-order prose float at the TOP RIGHT, sometimes over the top Hero row. (3) The skill/cost disappears instead of parking under Diao Chan. (4) First real Duel Attack gets stuck centrally rather than parking under its actual author. (5) A later Attack replaces the earlier Attack and Lust history altogether. Gameplay may work but **the unified UX2 Frame + proof-backed, actor-owned history does not**. **Beauty Outshining the Moon is NOT reviewed yet**; no UI-4 blanket acceptance.

**Design supersession:** The user rejected a full-width public turn/status bar under the top-row Heroes because it conflicts with their parked played cards. User-approved alternative is ONE **short, visually quiet translucent capsule at the LOWER BATTLEFIELD edge**, immediately ABOVE and OUTSIDE the Local Dock. This is distinct from **H4-A/B/C public event narration** centred on the battlefield: the capsule means *who publicly acts / what is pending*; H4 tells *what was committed*; LOCAL Guidance tells *what I personally must do*. A skill Frame is physically separate from the standing capsule. Do not reuse H4 copy/banner as turn-owner chip or move H4 back to upper-right.

#### 10.12.1 One persistent PUBLIC ACTIVITY CHIP — with privacy-safe ownership

**Precise content rules:**
- **Normal Play Phase:** \`Test Player 2's turn\`, derived from authoritative PUBLIC \`room.turnSeat\`/actual turn state, identical across independent viewers. Update on each true turn transition; don't repeat in Local Guidance.
- **Public Duel exchange / other PUBLIC single-actor response:** \`Waiting for Test Player 3 · Duel\` or \`Waiting for Test Player 4 · Attack\` ONLY if current actor and public action are proven by the shared server projection. Do not confuse original turn owner, activating Diao Chan and the next Duel responder.
- **Secret UX2 simultaneous Negation Plan A:** ALL clients see \`Waiting for Negation responses\`. Never publish any responder's name, submitted/pass state, response count, priority, card ownership or inferred Negation availability; not even when one player has already submitted. Existing 8s/all-explicit server settlement remains untouched.
- **No public actor proof / settling:** \`Resolving…\` or hide the capsule rather than infer from PRIVATE \`currentAction.reason\`, viewer-specific \`pendingNegation.submitted\` or client guesses. On game finished, show \`Match complete\` (or hide), not a stale player turn.
- **Full-time within game:** status persists and updates from authoritative room state during new turns and response phases for all viewers; it is not a 2.4-second toast. When no real change happens, no flicker.

**Projection/code:** Build a pure \`derivePublicActivityStatus\` on strictly PUBLIC room fields/\`PresentationV2\` or extend \`app/api/rooms/route.ts\` with an allowlisted \`publicActivity\` if current per-viewer room shape cannot guarantee identical data. Never drive a shared public label from \`buildDecisionPresentation\`'s viewer-private isWaiting/reason. Test identical public text on independent player tokens. Fail closed, and retain \`aria-live="polite"\` without announcing every poll.

**Geometry:** One-line content-sized badge, ~11–12px readable typography, ~22–30px height, subtle black/translucent background and thin gold border, \`pointer-events:none\`; NOT a full-width panel. Anchor at **bottom centre of \`.play-table\`**, above Local Guidance and left of bottom-right countdown as needed. Dynamically reserve actual occupied region for any local/side Seat-attached Duel/Negation history, public centre Frame, H4 announcement, equipment, controls and timer; if lower middle occupied use the nearest stable alternative **in the SAME lower public corridor**, not a top-of-table jump or overlay. Prefer shortening truthful copy to 1 line, avoid shrink-to-unreadable font or stretching. This chip must not follow a moving physical CardFace. Test 390×844/390×700/440×894/480×900 and 4/6/8/10 Seat topology. If space genuinely impossible, temporarily hide instead of cover essential controls, without losing authoritative status. Inspect actual bounding rectangles on mobile.

#### 10.15.5 Binding implementation contract — physical lifecycle, semantic checkpoint and viewer geometry are separate clocks

**Single-owner rule:** For one validated (roomCode, interactionId, rootFrameId, rootEventId, physicalCardId, actualAuthorId), only one **physical root presentation coordinator** may render the public root. It must persist across NEGATION, GROUP_RESOLUTION participant 1/2/3, damage, optional triggered skill and settlement, even when presentationRevision, checkpointId, participant, response timer, selection branch or notice changes. Build this linkage from PROVEN server/public relationships; never join by latest timeline item, card kind, player name or turnSeat. If evidence of the linkage is missing, fail closed rather than guess. Other unrelated card families may still use their generic fallback; a root already owned/parked by a Journey must **never** return through static fallback.

| Independent clock | Stable authority | Events allowed to change it | Forbidden side effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Physical event identity** | Proven root event + physical card + true author + typed interaction/frame proof | A different genuinely committed physical card | Duplicate or impersonated root |
| **Visual lifecycle** | Same physical event state: UNSEEN → REVEAL → MOVE → PARKED → RETIRED | First public commitment, normal ≈4s reveal, ≈380ms move, real interrupt or retirement | PARKED→REVEAL from a new checkpoint, response, poll or switching viewers |
| **Semantic checkpoint** | PROVEN interaction/decision/current participant/settlement | Server advances group target, Negation, damage, outcome | Restart visual root or move already parked root |
| **Viewer layout epoch** | Viewer ID + measured Seat/Dock/topology + visualViewport | TEST SWITCH, reconnect, resize/rotation, topology changes | Old-view-to-new-view flying animation; wrong author |
| **Public narration** | Latest proven public stage/event copy via H4 | Genuine server-proven semantic stage change | Text follows shrinking root, stale previous-stage notice, false private reveal |

**Q2 / state ownership:** extend one typed Group-root Journey throughout normal Group response and GROUP_RESOLVED, including phases where Negation is not active. Preserve existing exact source/root/card/frame proof, root actor identity, historical genuine Negations and distinct physical response cards. A genuinely NEW committed response card may reveal at centre and interrupt the root; the old root remains PARKED. The old root must not be reselected as a new central event by an unrelated target response or settlement result. Implement arbitration once at a shared presenter boundary, not separately per group stage. Do not merely hide CSS static cards while still mounting duplicate physical owners.

**Q3 / first-paint view barrier:** visual phase/commit history belongs to the root, while layout coordinates belong to the CURRENT viewer. On TEST SWITCH or legitimate layout-epoch change, reproject already PARKED roots to the new measured true-author anchor BEFORE first paint, with transition disabled. Do not animate from cached actualCardRect belonging to another viewer, do not flash at stale coordinates and do not replay 4s because an event is new to the observer. If new anchor is unmeasurable, postpone that card's painting rather than use 0,0 or guess. A newly confirmed physical card in the same, unchanged view still gets the accepted 4s/380ms motion. Test on Attack/Dodge, Duel/Lust and other Journey types too, while keeping Q3 a separate bounded task.

**Q4 / H4 independent public caption:** use one stage-fixed, safely located PublicCardAnnouncement band, sourced only from up-to-date proven public checkpoints. It may change copy as response windows genuinely advance; it must not change its position because a card shrinks, parks or a timer ticks. Retire old-stage copy as soon as authoritative semantic scope changes (e.g. no leftover "Negation can be played" during Group response); do not reveal private submissions. Measure the actual newly deployed H4 implementation, accept existing H3 font/copy, and preserve USER-ACCEPTED U13-B activity chip. H4 centre deviation ≤12px and vertical movement ≤16px apply under unchanged safe geometry; avoid top Seats, current central/parked physical cards, timer, Local Dock and chip.

**Q1 instrumentation additions:** privacy-reviewed diagnostic trace should log paired PROVEN server and presenter IDs and this public-only record per render checkpoint: build SHA, session ID, monotonic elapsed time, room/interaction/frame/checkpoint/revision, root event/card/author, current participant, current viewer/layout epoch, rendererKind/motionType/visualPhase, reveal/move start and elapsed, number + DOM path/rect of every SAME-root full/parked instance, last viewer rect versus current anchor rect, H4 notice event/semantic stage/text key + rect, safe stage/obstacle rects. Redact all private Hand identities, other players' Negation availability/intents, credentials, secret roles. Instrument ahead of behavior changes and avoid treating presentationRevision as a new physical-card identity.
