#### 10.15.6 Executable three-surface presentation specification — MUST / MUST NOT (2026-10-17 clarification)

**P0 user requirement in one sentence:** For the **same proven real card**, the (A) central full-sized card, (B) returned small author-attached card and (C) shared public explanatory text must describe one coherent public event across time and viewpoints; they must not independently restart, move between owners, disagree, or resurrect old stages. This section is **normative over cosmetic placement preferences** and can be handed directly to the Coding Agent. The problem is **presentation arbitration and rehydration, not changes to the WTK rules or CurrentAction**.

**Three surfaces have distinct jobs and must NEVER compete for authority:**

| Surface | When it exists | Where it belongs | Exactly what it may display | What it must NEVER do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Centre REVEAL / MOVE CardFace** | Only for a **newly committed, server-proven physical card** whose event has not already completed its current viewer's reveal/move lifecycle; newer committed cards may interrupt | Central battlefield safe reveal area, then animate toward true author | ONE current full-size real card with real card ID, owner and event ID | Rerender an old parked root because the group advances to the next target; invent a second root from settlement; run again after TEST SWITCH/poll/refresh |
| **B. PARKED miniature/history** | The same physical event after MOVE, or immediately on viewing already-committed history after switching/late joining/reconnecting | Actual **author's** Seat or own Dock in this observer's current topology (global chronological ordering retained) | The same real physical card, shrunk once, with genuine ordinal when applicable | Fly from a previous observer's seat; change owner; grow back into a centre card; disappear merely because next participant must answer |
| **C. Public event narration (H4)** | While there is a **current, proven public stage/event** requiring a shared explanation; update or retire as proven semantic stage changes | Its **own fixed central safe reading band** (not a child of the card's position/transform) | Current proven actor, action, target, response or outcome text; accepted H3 typography/copy | Follow A or B; lag with a prior Negation/target message; duplicate a separate generic toast; overlap A/B, player HP, response countdown, Dock or accepted U13-B status plaque |

**Strict state-transition contract for one root:**

~~~text
PROVEN NEW ROOT [event/card/author] -> REVEAL(max 4000ms by Policy B)
                                  -> MOVE(about 380ms, to THIS viewer's true-author anchor)
                                  -> PARKED (same real card; stay parked through all target decisions)
                                  -> RETIRED (only when proven history-display policy retires it)

PARKED + target-2/3 response = PARKED (no large re-display)
PARKED + GROUP_RESOLVED      = PARKED (no new static large card)
PARKED + presentationRevision/checkpoint changes = PARKED
PARKED + TEST SWITCH / resize = PARKED at recalculated destination, SNAP WITHOUT TRANSITION
PARKED + poll / reconnect / remount = PARKED, never replay by default
NEW different committed response card = its OWN new centre lifecycle; prior root stays PARKED

C: Proven public semantic stage N -> stage N+1 = replace/retire stage-N text;
   C position remains in its safe band and is not coupled to A/B transforms.
~~~

**Timing and interruption:** The intended REVEAL hold is **up to approximately 4 seconds**, and MOVE about **380ms**, not an unconditional 4-second blocking delay. A newer, *genuinely committed and publicly proven* response may interrupt the prior centre reveal; no purely local response intent or transient UI checkpoint may do so. No new card? Then no fresh REVEAL. A network poll, target index advance, damage/skill settlement, stage revision or visual viewport change is **not** a new physical commitment. Reduced-motion users see equivalent identity/placement without forced flight. Do not infer timing/ownership from a DOM timer.

**Cross-player contract using the recorded genuine Barbarian root:**

| State / viewer | Expected A centre | Expected B miniature | Expected C narration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Viewer 0 first sees root 76af7aee… newly committed | One initial REVEAL, then MOVE | Same root parks under actual source 72383b7b… | Initial **server-proven** public root/action message; H4 safe band |
| Viewer 0 watches target 2, then target 3 respond | **No second root** at centre (new genuine response CardFaces only if proved) | Root d7478792… remains under that same author | Text advances to the newly proven response/target; previous text removed |
| TEST SWITCH viewer 0→1→2→3 during group response | **No root REVEAL restart** | Same physical root **snaps directly** to each new viewer's measured author Seat/Dock, zero flight from prior layout | Current public semantic message reprojects into the viewer's **own safe H4 band**, does not trail the card |
| Group settles | **No 88×128px old-root static fallback** | Root history remains on true author until normal proven retirement | Only current group settlement outcome; obsolete response/Negation message gone |
| Newly connected independent client after root was already public | **No historical replay as fresh commitment** | Reconstructed parked root in the actual author slot according to the existing history policy | Latest proven public stage, not delayed or cached private copy |

**Renderer exclusivity is a functional requirement, not a styling tweak:** At any observation of a given physical root, the system must have a **single effective visual owner** (one typed Journey rather than Journey competing with static-fallback). No full-size static root CardFace is permitted once that root is PARKED, even if a Group settlement produces a different action object; no CSS-only hiding of a duplicate which is still independently driving stale notice state. Display identity must use proven interaction/root/card/author linkage and **must not depend on** checkpointId, presentationRevision, current target seat, current player name, current viewerId or DOM coordinates. Those fields can update **semantics** or **layout**, not reset the root's visual clock.

**Presentation and geometry must be separated:** The root's logical phase/event history survives updates. On a viewerId/Seat topology/visualViewport change, invalidate old coordinates, measure new DOM anchors, and suppress transitions **before painting** any already parked historical card. A client may have one viewer-relative position per layout epoch, but may NEVER interpolate from previous-view x=338px to new-view x=196px for an already PARKED card. If current true-author anchor is unavailable, wait/withhold rendering; never guess location/owner. Same rule applies to legacy Attack/Dodge, Negation, Duel/Lust and other real physical card Journeys, without expanding Q2 beyond Group roots.

**Public narration freshness:** The H4 text's semantic event ID/checkpoint must track current **PROVEN** server interaction state. At confirmed advance, replace the prior stage's visible copy atomically: e.g. “Waiting for Negation” cannot linger when response ownership has advanced to a proven group target; “target 1 responded” cannot still be the visible current instruction while target 2 is acting. The narration's placement is determined by a safe stage band; it must not be recalculated from A's shrinking card or B's parked anchor. When geometry changes (e.g. viewer switch) the safe band may legitimately reproject, but under **unchanged layout** its centre drifts no more than 12px horizontally and 16px vertically. Preserve the separate USER-ACCEPTED U13-B bottom activity chip; H4 provides *event meaning*, U13-B provides *whose action is awaited*.

**Source evidence vs current release:** The uploaded old-build aa71e75 trace proves root REVEAL t=72.729, MOVE t=76.791, PARKED t=77.162, then later same-root full card sightings at t≈87.79 and 116.63; TEST SWITCH records x=338.3→196→53.7→14 for the same parked root. This evidence **does not by itself certify present H4 malfunction** or real four-client simultaneity. Audit the **deployed new SHA**. From latest source, untyped normal Group/settlement candidates and PublicCardDisplay static-fallback remain the main Q1/Q2 suspects; do not claim a bug fixed by specification alone.

**Concrete Coding Agent acceptance gate, not optional:**

1. **Q1 (current only):** Diagnose and log ONE root's stable `rootEventId`, `physicalCardId`, `actualAuthorId`, `interactionId`, `rootFrameId` from PROVEN server projection to chosen renderer, with `rendererKind`, `motionType`, `visualPhase`, `viewer/layoutEpoch` and all same-physical-card DOM paths/rects. At each target step confirm narration semantics, only one current H4 banner, fixed safe position, no collision with card/history, top Seats, timers, hand and U13-B chip.

Capture matched **real event/card/author IDs** across clients for Barbarian Invasion **and** Raining Arrows through ≥3 actual target responses, Negation, damage and final settlement; separately test viewer switch both during initial reveal and after park, late join/refresh/resize, long names and small phones (390×700, 390×844, captured 440×766, 440×894, 480×900). **Boundaries:** This specification authorizes **presentation** fixes only. Existing game's verified decisions, exact physical-card conservation, shared Negation Plan A, accepted H3 and U13-B, reveal interruption and real chronological author parking remain intact. #### 10.18.1 ST5-1 — five-seat ring/edge layout; **USER-ACCEPTED / CLOSED** (2026-10-23 22:03 UTC; 5/5 phone checks)

**Original owner phone re-review (2026-10-22 23:08–23:19 UTC) — failure evidence, subsequently corrected:** iPhone screenshots `IMG_3559.jpeg`/`IMG_3560.jpeg`/`IMG_3561.jpeg` at 440px showed compact opponent rows delivered, but four Seats sat too far inward and the left-side sequence broke the visible ring order. The implementation and acceptance criteria below preserve this diagnosis and the required upper-row compactness regression. Current technical status is recorded after the criteria; the owner has not yet re-reviewed the new deployment.

**Trace evidence and server boundary:** `wtk-game-ux-trace-2026-10-22T23-08-21.176Z.json` is a complete session (0 dropped entries), viewer viewport 440×766, DPR3, device JS build `7e14307eff6af1ab917666b6fc1aa409df96ab61`; earlier entries refer to a different restored 4-player game, but the new session after `add_test_players` is exactly FIVE alive seats: Cao Cao local server Seat 0, Sima Yi Seat 1, Xiahou Dun Seat 2, Zhang Liao Seat 3 and Xu Zhu Seat 4. No submitted illegal Attack is evidenced by this trace, so screenshot button states are stronger evidence than claiming a failed server POST. Source audit at remote `ux-v2` SHA `038176ba9ed489d24c5c760d628d9cab467bd233`. Refresh current head/branch/last-effective CSS at implementation time.

**CONFIRMED first cause — inconsistent circular physical order, not server distance:** `app/page.tsx:projectSideColumnSeat(totalPlayers,relativeIndex)` defines `rightCount=ceil((N-1)/2)`, `leftCount=N-1-rightCount`, and RIGHT `row=rightCount-relativeIndex+1` (so relative Seat 1 is bottom-right nearest the local Dock). LEFT currently uses `row=leftCount-(relativeIndex-rightCount)+1`, reversing the left edge ALSO bottom-to-top. With N=5, current screen maps `relative 1→right row2, 2→right row1, 3→left row2, 4→left row1`, so physical clockwise reading skips one seat across the top. Required contiguous ring: `1→right row2, 2→right row1, 3→left row1, 4→left row2`. Local neighbours 1 and 4 must be the BOTTOM right and BOTTOM left opponents; middle-distance opponents 2 and 3 are the UPPER pair. The underlying `serverSeat`, `player.id`, distance projection, turn order and click ownership are already correct and MUST NOT change. Existing `tests/browser/side-column-seat-recognition.spec.mjs` incorrectly EXPECTS the old left row inversion (its `expected` map has relative3 left row2 / relative4 left row1), therefore green tests do not establish the desired ring.

**MANDATORY mathematical mapping implementation:** Keep the right-row rule; change the LEFT mapping to begin at the upper remaining row and proceed down to the local neighbour, e.g. `row = (rightCount - leftCount) + (relativeIndex - rightCount)` for relativeIndex > rightCount. This intentionally bottom-aligns the nearer left Seat even when counts differ (N=6: right rows 3,2,1 for relative1..3; left rows 2,3 for relative4..5); do not naively use `row=relativeIndex-rightCount` for ALL side-column counts, because an odd number of opponents leaves the left-nearest Seat one row above the right-nearest. Derive the expected 5/6/7/8/9/10 lookup examples from the above formula, assert exact one Seat per claimed side/row and contiguous circular ordering. If a higher-count layout has a separately accepted conflicting arrangement, document the collision and scope the initial runtime rule to count=5 pending owner decision; do NOT silently change previously accepted 6–10 placements. Distances must NEVER be computed from visual row/column or pixel positions.

#### 10.19.1 Required visible Option A, exact language contract

**ONE authoritative visible H4 narrator, not a second modal or new permanent information pane.** Reuse the already user-accepted centred `PublicCardAnnouncement` / `.public-card-display-journey-copy` stage-fixed safe band. Present an emphasized immediate **event line** (actor → exact countered event) plus a **current-effect line** (ACTIVE/BLOCKED, with explicit pending/final distinction). Large enough to be noticed (~15–16px event headline with ~13–14px supporting line on baseline phones; derive final fit from computed mobile geometry), dark/gold existing WTK styling, optional subtle colour/status icon but **never colour as the only meaning**. Display just the latest relevant committed event plus current status; the genuine accepted numbered Seat/Dock minis remain the chronological public physical history. DO NOT create a new sidebar, stacked modal, scrolling log, enormous EFFECT window, arrows/connectors, new causal graph or persistent duplicate top/bottom toast.

**Normative four-step example (fictional names, substitute ONLY real public-proven player names and card identity):**

| Proven stage | H4 event headline / concise public text | H4 supporting current-effect line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root Duel committed: Zhang Liao → Guan Yu | `Zhang Liao played Duel on Guan Yu.` | `Negation response open · Duel not yet resolved.` |
| Real Negation #1 by Cao Cao, directly against root Duel | `Cao Cao's Negation counters Zhang Liao's Duel.` | `Duel currently BLOCKED · Counter-Negation still possible.` |
| Real Negation #2 by Sun Quan, directly against Cao Cao's Negation | `Sun Quan counters Cao Cao's Negation.` | `Duel currently ACTIVE · Another Negation is possible.` |
| Real Negation #3 by Liu Bei, directly against Sun Quan's Negation | `Liu Bei counters Sun Quan's Negation.` | `Duel currently BLOCKED · Another Negation is possible.` |

**Compact mobile copy** may use `Negation #2: Sun Quan counters Cao Cao.` + `Duel ACTIVE · Response open`, provided **both source/countered participant and the nature of the countered Negation** remain understandable. If the server confirms the **final no-new-counter settlement**, replace provisional copy with a truthful final notice, e.g. `FINAL · Duel cancelled — no Duel Attack exchange.` (odd genuine chain and confirmed cancelled) or `FINAL · Duel proceeds — Guan Yu responds with Attack.` (even genuine chain and confirmed Duel continuation). The latter must only be used if the actual server-confirmed continuation indeed calls for that response; otherwise say `Duel takes effect.` **NEVER say “damage dealt” or a victor until separate proven Duel settlement.** Do not display a FINAL label merely because a private player pressed Pass, the 8s timer visually reached 0, a 4s card reveal ended, or the client recomputed odd/even parity.

**Truth semantics:**
- A published Negation #1 counters the ROOT effect; #2 counters the PREVIOUS PUBLIC Negation; #3 counters #2; and so forth. Attribute the *immediate* target honestly. `rootEffectState` parity (odd BLOCKED, even ACTIVE) is a consistency CHECK, not a substitute for matching the actual public event chain.
- During an active/new shared Negation window, `ACTIVE` and `BLOCKED` mean **CURRENT/PROVISIONAL**, NOT finally resolved; do not claim “Duel will hit”, “canceled forever” or “card damage prevented” when a further counter or Duel Attack exchange is pending.
- A private selected/submitted/losing Negation intent is **NOT an event**, must not change H4, step count, current effect or create an animated public CardFace. After the server chooses ONE winning public Negation from an 8-second MAX shared window (or earlier all-living-seats-explicit response), that committed winner alone advances the visible step. Each new public counter opens a new authoritative window. All viewers see the SAME public stage even if their private local `CurrentAction` differs.
- Group/ordered target exceptions: if an existing stratagem is countered for ONE specific target, describe `effect on [proven recipient]` rather than incorrectly saying the whole multi-target root is cancelled. Preserve the user's accepted special Harvest phrasing/labels unchanged in this first NEG-A1 slice.
- On missing, nonunique or stale proof, show a NEUTRAL existing public `Negation response open / awaiting resolution` fallback, without invented player names, card rank/suit, effect state, counter ancestry or FINAL. The existing accepted source/target H4 or activity chip is preferable to a false explanation.

4. **Make end-of-hold advancement self-healing.** Replace single-fire, fail-forever scheduling with a *bounded-rate, non-overlapping* completion watcher keyed to `room.code` + **server-authoritative** `pendingHarvest.complete` + `countdownUntil` (and changed room/interaction identity when available). Do not hammer D1 or spin `setTimeout(0)`, retry gameplay decisions, produce duplicate final messages, revive an inactive game, or accept a local clock as proof. If a retry keeps failing, record non-sensitive diagnostic and allow the normal server-validated next attempt; owner may see a restrained "Finishing result…" status but no fake timer or bogus Confirm button.

### 10.20 TGT-A1 — immediate authoritative invalid-target rejection; **USER-ACCEPTED / CLOSED** (2026-10-23 22:03 UTC; 8/8 phone checks)

**Owner UX requirement (2026-10-22 23:17 UTC onward):** While the local player is selecting a target for Attack OR any other target-requiring card, clicking a target which the CURRENT authoritative action does not allow MUST NOT (a) highlight it as selected, (b) append it to targetIds or preview, (c) enable Confirm, or (d) send a gameplay request. The SAME TAP instead puts a concise contextual explanation into the **existing Local Player Dock/operation console guidance region**. For true distance rejection: **`Cannot attack Zhang Liao — distance 2; Attack range 1.`** For a card-specific range: **`Cannot use Steal on Zhang Liao — distance 2; Steal range 1.`** For restriction unrelated to distance, show the REAL reason, not a fabricated range. The target remains independently Inspect-able through its existing information control. This is a NEW separate target-selection experience design, not a re-opening of accepted Bumper Harvest/H4/Inspector or a server game-rule change.

**CONFIRMED client defect (at 2026-10-23 `ux-v2` source):**
- `app/page.tsx` `cardTargetLegal` only checks `game/capabilities/targeting.ts:canTargetCharacter` and Borrowed Sword holder eligibility. **Attack effective distance is NOT evaluated here.** `targetablePlayer` therefore sets gold actionable status for a living target at distance 2 even when local Attack range is 1.
- `OpponentPlayerCard` derives `targetButtonDisabled = targetSelectionActive && (!targetablePlayer || !player.alive)`. For some actually illegal modes the button is disabled and offers no tap explanation; for OUT-OF-RANGE Attack it remains enabled and `onTarget` reaches `setTarget(player.id)`. That setter mutates `targetIds` without an authoritative Attack range/target check, and the handler also automatically calls `openOpponentInspection` even for an illegal selection attempt.
- Only LATER does `attackTargetsValid` compare server-projected `player.distance <= me.attackRange`, disabling `Confirm` and blocking `play()`. Other card modes such as `Steal` and `RationsDepleted` have server `stratagemRangeAllowed` validation but the client selection/Confirm path does not consistently apply that constraint. The screenshots show a disabled Confirm after an illegal selection; this code flow explains it.
- **Server authority is already present/correct for this example:** `game/rules.ts:distanceBetween` computes circular shortest living-seat distance; `effectiveDistanceBetween` calls `game/capabilities/distance.ts:resolveEffectiveDistance` for horses and Hero modifiers; `app/api/rooms/route.ts:attackDistance` projects the effective distance and `attackRangeFor` projects Attack reach. Server `play_card` checks `attackDistance > attackRangeFor` before acceptance, `serpent_spear_attack` does likewise; `Steal`/`RationsDepleted` use `stratagemRangeAllowed` (including relevant range-ignoring capabilities). **NEVER calculate attack distance from physical UI coordinates, and NEVER weaken/replace server POST validation.**
- Architectural boundary: `AGENTS.md` requires **CurrentAction viewer-local legality authority**, not React rebuilding card rules from `player.distance` alone. Existing `game/protocol.d.ts:CurrentAction` has `canDeclareAttack`, `playPhaseActions` and selected special target lists, but **does not currently publish a complete eligible target/rejection reason projection for ordinary targeted play cards**. Do NOT solve this by copying the server’s many card/range checks into a new client-side target if/else tree.

**Preferred server-authoritative design (bounded, reusable; protocol extension only, not rule change):**
1. Build ONE shared server-side target eligibility evaluator that can be called by BOTH the authoritative `play_card` / `serpent_spear_attack` validation and the read-only `roomState` projection. Use current server data: alive circular Seats, `attackDistance()`, `attackRangeFor()`, `canTargetCharacter()`, `stratagemRangeAllowed()`, target card count/weapon/delayed-zone predicates. The evaluator returns per local `cardId` or virtual Attack mode a bounded set of allowed `targetId` values and, for visible target IDs, **a stable reason code** on rejection: `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `TARGET_RESTRICTED`, `NO_TARGETABLE_CARDS`, `DUPLICATE_DELAYED_CARD`, `NOT_ELIGIBLE`, `ACTION_UNAVAILABLE`; specific, demonstrable publicly explainable distance/range for `OUT_OF_RANGE` only. Unknown state fails closed without inventing a reason. Preserve special `CurrentAction.triggerOptions.selection.targetIds`, active-skill eligible targets and `borrowedSwordTargets` rather than replacing them.
2. Add an **optional owner-private presentation field** to `game/protocol.d.ts:CurrentAction` (e.g. `playTargetEligibility`, keyed by actual physical `cardId` plus **effective playable kind**, or explicit virtual `serpent_spear_attack` mode). Extend only the current actor's `roomState` projection in `app/api/rooms/route.ts`; other viewers/TEST SWITCH spectators must not receive that viewer’s private playable Hand data. No D1 migration, new HTTP route, new server actions or change of `CurrentAction.version=3` needed for optional backwards-compatible field. Guard against stale `actionRevision` and mismatched card/viewer; preserve server revalidation upon submit. The existing `player.distance` and `attackRange` are optional **explanation facts** (already server-computed), NEVER independent fallback legal authority.
3. Cover ordinary Attack, legal Attack-as-converted physical cards (Guan Yu red Attack, Zhao Yun Dodge→Attack), Serpent Spear two-card virtual Attack, Sky Piercing Halberd multiple target selection, plus distance-sensitive `Steal`/`RationsDepleted` and ordinary targeted `Duel`, `Dismantle`, `Overindulgence`, `BorrowedSword`. Important distinctions: `Duel` and `Dismantle` must not be rejected merely because effective Attack range=1; `Steal`/`RationsDepleted` use THEIR card range, not current Attack weapon range; legitimate passive range-ignore capabilities (e.g. Wizardry) must still work even if `effectiveDistance > ordinaryRange`. Target eligibility must also account for restrictions and target-specific card/Equipment facts, not merely distance.
4. In `app/page.tsx` separate a **normal target tap attempt** from mutation: `attemptTarget(playerId,currentMode)` obtains the CURRENT `CurrentAction` eligibility verdict BEFORE `setTarget`, `setTargetIds`, selection CSS, Inspector auto-open or choice preview. #### 10.22.1 User-visible contract

- **Reference:** Accepted Harvest's compact gold/black bounded panel, accurate full usable Hand-size CardFace geometry, real art/suit/rank, independent bottom-centre Info for genuine public cards, one horizontal browsing row, readable title/instruction, actor-only selected state and a compact pinned action footer. The card-pool UI fits **inside a measured battlefield safety corridor just below true opponent Seats and as high as safely feasible**, not default `align-items:flex-end` at battlefield bottom and not a fullscreen modal. It avoids H4, public activity chip, visible countdown/system cluster, Inspector, legal seat controls, Local Dock and Hand. Five-seat side-lane compensation is essential. Use horizontal row scroll rather than smaller card art or panel expansion to display more cards.
- **Same frame, different proof:** Harvest presents server-PUBLIC revealed cards and confirmed Taken/Available status; only the authentic current chooser selects. Steal/Burning Bridge present PRIVATE actor-only eligible selections, where an opposing Hand stays anonymous, while genuine target Equipment/Judgement has publicly-proven identity. The *frame* is reusable; a common React component must never merge the two data authorities or expose hidden identities via a generic `Card` prop to spectators. Every effect adapter retains its own current actor, permissions, min/max, legal keys, action revision, deadlines, submit/mutation/error handling and ownership of outcomes.
- **Conditional zone switcher, approved by owner:** One nonempty eligible zone => one row, no tab bar. Two or three nonempty zones => compact accessible `HAND / EQUIPMENT / JUDGEMENT` tabs, with truthful counts and **only the active zone's single card row rendered/visible**, no HAND+EQUIPMENT vertical stacking. Changing tabs does NOT change selected card or server state; selected-zone note visible when selected card is off-tab. Tap selected card again to deselect, new legal one-card selection replaces previous choice, obey min/max for other future adapters. One server-proven random Hand key `hand` displays **one random-zone selector** plus count; never fabricate N independent hand-position choices. A server-proven positional `hand:N` remains an anonymous positional selector.
- **Shared touch / action:** Info is independent of selection (and only on publicly known real cards); 44px-class reachable tap area if feasible without covering adjacent card; focus returns to same item. Footer Confirm/Use is clearly reachable without page scrolling even 390×700; only horizontally browsable row can scroll. No redundant Cancel/Clear on mandatory choice, no Skip unless server-authorized. Nonmodal pointer pass-through outside panel keeps authorized SWITCH, player Inspector and spectator board controls usable. Read-only spectator mode has **zero** selectable card/Confirm, not merely disabled controls overlaying public cards.

## 11. UX3 FUTURE backlog — Negation Plan B, immediate-public-on-Confirm (NOT AN UX2 TASK)

**User preference recorded 2026-10-14 (future UX3 only):** Explore individual immediate-public Negation Confirm through a separately approved future UX3 design. This is NOT authorized autonomous UX2 work. UX2 Negation Plan A remains private all-seat submission, maximum 8s and early server settlement only after EVERY living seat explicitly responds.

**Non-trivial unresolved tradeoff:** UX2 private simultaneous intents still use canonical seat priority; all-seats explicit early completion doesn't change that. Immediately displaying an INDIVIDUAL's Confirm as a PUBLIC card, while others remain undecided, could expose a losing intent, consume a wrong card or leak secret availability. UX3 requires a separately approved authoritative arbitration rule, not an optimistic animation or simply changing the 8s maximum.

**UX3 questions to design with user before authorization:** (1) first-arrival commitment versus stable clockwise seat priority / override grace window; (2) protecting opponent Negation availability and private Hand when no card is submitted; (3) new counter windows, timeouts, fairness under network lag and reconnect; (4) atomic exactly-once actual card consumption, conflicting simultaneous confirms, Duel/Group/Judgement consistency; (5) visible chronological author-attached card history, animation interruption, old-save migration, rollbacks and authenticated multi-viewer privacy tests.

**Separate UX3 design decision, not an UX2 review gate:** UX3 needs distinct product/rules authorization because it changes priority, privacy and fairness. Continue all approved UX2 work without awaiting acceptance of prior UX2 items, but do not silently implement this unapproved UX3 rule.
